findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_lux_reading_questions" stacks urgency/override words (important, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_wait_times · Private data: get_export_guide, get_count_link, get_inference_file, how_to_see_what_a_platform_knows, get_lux_reading_questions · Public sink: get_count_link.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_wait_times · Private data: get_export_guide, get_count_link, get_inference_file, how_to_see_what_a_platform_knows, get_lux_reading_questions · Public sink: get_count_link

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_wait_times" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "How long each platform’s personal data export takes from request to ready, plus the download window, for 11 platforms in one table. Every figure is labeled reported (from the platform’s own help text, with source) or measured (our own request and ready timestamps). Source page: https://pupulcorp.com" → after: "How long a platform’s personal data export takes from request to ready, plus the download window and the limit the platform itself states. Pass a platform to get only that platform’s rows, which is what you want when answering one question; omit it for all 17 rows across 11 platforms. Every row come"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
